summary: Explains how the legacy key=value syntax (used in ad hoc commands) parses backslash escapes regardless of quoting, so backslashes should be escaped; unescaped paths can turn \t into a TAB character.
questions: How do I write Windows paths in ad hoc key=value arguments?
Why did my path become C:\Windows<TAB>emp?
Does quoting matter in Ansible's key=value syntax?

answer_card.title: Windows paths in key=value syntax
answer_card.answer_md:
In `key=value` form (ad hoc commands or inline in playbooks), quoting has **no effect** on parsing, and backslash escapes like `\t`, `\n`, `\x..` are interpreted. Escape backslashes:

```ini
# GOOD
tempdir=C:\\Windows\\Temp
# FAILS (\t becomes TAB -> C:\Windows<TAB>emp)
tempdir=C:\Windows\temp
```

This style is discouraged in playbooks because of the escaping.
